paragraphs: Yishmael of Kefar Yama; some say, of Kefar Dima.
Mentioned in Nedarim 57b: he brought a question before Rabbi Ami, who had no answer. He came before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, who resolved it for him.

notes.text: The idioms describe bringing a question, Ami having no answer and Yitzchak Nappacha resolving it; they do not describe carrying something in a hand.

Hyman supplies ‘a question’ in parentheses, which is the scope of the earlier note’s idiomatic rendering. The fuller consulted Nedarim account explicitly mentions an onion and spells the alternative place name Dyama.
